title: The long-term outcome of the Kasai operation in patients with biliary atresia: a systematic review.
abstract: Biliary atresia (BA) is a progressive inflammatory destructive process of the bile ducts occurring in about one of every 20,000 live births. If left untreated, biliary atresia can lead to liver failure. The only effective treatments for BA at the moment are the Kasai operation and liver transplantation. Kasai portoenterostomy increases the survival of children with BA and postpones subsequent liver transplantation. Because long-term survival is rare, there is not much known about the long-term efficacy of the Kasai operation.
